notes.title: Demo Patch Notes 0.4.006
notes.content:
Hi there! ~~🎉👋 

We hope you’re having fun with the Demo!


In this patch, we’re introducing several system reworks, texture and animation updates, and a new Crimson Knight ability.

[h1]Major Changes[/h1]
[list]
[*] Added new Animation + VFX to Crimson Knight's abilities
[*] Added new Crimson Knight Ability: [b]Bloodshatter[/b]
[*] Reworked Tenderize to summon a Void Vortex that travels forwards
[*] Reworked the looting system. Enemies and destructible objects will now drop a pouch containing all their loot on the ground, which can then be picked up.
[list]
[*] [i]Dev Note: With this looting systems, players can now inspect items before picking them up.[/i][/list][*] New Stat added: [b]Skill[/b][list]
[*] Skill is a new implicit modifier that combines the old implicit modifiers namely Life, Power, Essence and Armor into [b]one [/b]Stat. 
[/list][*] All proc-based modifiers have been grouped into a new category called [b]Extra Effect Modifiers[/b], indicated by a pink circle in the Equipment inspect window
[*] Lowered the amount of modifiers on Equipments
[list]
[*] Common: 0 Prefixes and 0 Suffixes
[*] Rare: Either 1 Prefix or 1 Suffix
[*] Epic: 1 Prefix and 1 Suffix
[*] Heirloom: Either 1 Prefix and 2 Suffixes or 2 Prefixes and 1 Suffix (Has a chance to roll an additional Effect Modifier)
[*] Legendary: 2 Prefixes and 2 Suffixes (Has a chance to roll an additional Effect Modifier)
[*] Mythical: 2 Prefixes and 2 Suffixes (Has a chance to roll up to two additional Effect Modifiers)
[*] [i]Dev Note: Loading old save files will transform your old Equipments to feature the new modifier system. That being said, the Equipments will still feature the same amount of modifiers they had with the old system (so you will not lose any modifiers). Any Equipments dropped from that point onwards will follow the new system.[/i]
[/list][*] Resistance Rework:
[list]
[*] Fire, Frost and Lightning Resistance have been merged into Elemental Resistance
[*] Corruption Resistance has been removed
[*] New Resistance: [b]Abyssal Resistance[/b]
[/list][*] Damage Type Rework:
[list]
[*] Fire, Frost and Lightning damage now grant Elemental damage
[*] Bleed damage has been converted into Physical damage
[list]
[*] [i]Dev Note: Many players thought bleed damage scales off physical damage which caused a lot of confusion, that's why we are simplifying things and merging them into one damage type.[/i]
[/list][*] Corruption Damage has been removed
[/list][*] Updated the textures of Molten Depths
[/list]


[h1]Balance Changes[/h1]
[list]
[*][b]Reduced the amount of Equipments that drop by 25%[/b]
[*][b]Adventure-mode health and damage scaling increased by 43%[/b]
[*][b]Buffed non-boss enemy damage by 10%[/b]
[*] [b]Flamebound Guardian[/b]
Health increased by 12%
Prophecy of Flames damage buffed by 50%
Ruination damage buffed by 25%
[*][b]They Who Hid[/b]
Health increased by 10% in Phase 1
[*][b]Condensed Darkness[/b]
Health increased by 33%
Movement Speed increased by 15%
[*][b]Fiend[/b]
Removed indicator on Tantrum
Reduced damage of Tantrum by 33%
[*][b]Corruptor[/b]
Health reduced by 15%
[*][b]Nerfed chest inherit item quantity by 50%[/b]
[*][b]Nerfed chest chance to roll Equipments by 25%[/b]
[/list]


[h1]Bug Fixes and Minor Changes[/h1]

[h3][b]Minor Changes[/b][/h3]
[list]
[*]Enemy Health Bars now display buffs
[*]Updated the lighting inside the Charred Woods, Molten Depths and The Discard
[*]Updated some monster SFX
[/list]

[h3][b]Bug Fixes[/b][/h3]
[list]
[*]Fixed an issue where enemy health bars would not display stacks of debuffs properly
[*]Beta Tester Crown should only be available via a valid Beta Tester Key (sorry for the confusion)
[*]Fixed a bug where Felya would not spawn after killing Magmadon for the first time
[*]Fixed a bug where adventure mode was scaling much more aggressively than intended
[*]Fixed a bug that caused old saves to lose certain Equipements
[*]Fixed a bug that made "Velkash, Grips of the Shattered Host" unobtainable
[*]Fixed a bug where Epics and Rares would not keep their names after loading a save file
[*]Many other small bug fixes
[/list]


Wishing you all the best
[i]Bardh & Burim[/i]

notes.title: [System Spotlight] Relic & Soul Crystals
notes.content:
Hello, world! 👋

Welcome back to the second post in our System Spotlight series! In this series, we'll be diving into some of the core mechanics that bring Sil and the Fading World to life.

This time around, we’ll be taking a closer look at the Relic & Soul Crystal system — a powerful feature that gives you deep control over your character’s build and playstyle. Let’s dive in.


[h1]🏺 Relic — A Vessel of Power[/h1]
At the heart of this system is the Relic, a one-of-a-kind piece of equipment that serves as a vessel for Soul Crystals. Unlike traditional gear, the Relic is unique and there are no variations or alternate versions. Every player will have access to the same Relic, but its true strength comes from the Soul Crystals you choose to slot into it.

Once slotted, Soul Crystals are activated automatically, effectively turning the Relic into a customizable MMO-style trinket that triggers powerful effects during combat.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45068931/f1b60fbd13b1cb241f1e42e1b18365005e7fdd4b.png[/img]

[h1]💎 Soul Crystals – Fragments of Slain Souls[/h1]
Soul Crystals are fragments of the souls of fallen enemies — crystallized splinters of their essence. Each Soul Crystal holds a specific ability or effect that can be triggered when certain conditions are met.

[h3]Conditions & Effects[/h3]
Every Soul Crystal is defined by two key elements:

[list]
[*] [b]Condition[/b]– The specific trigger that needs to be met for the effect to activate. Conditions can be tied to your actions, enemy behavior, or combat outcomes. Here are a couple examples:[list]
[*]"10% chance to spawn X when applying a bleed to an enemy."
[*]"25% chance on critical strike to deal AoE damage."
[*]"30% Chance when you block an attack to increase armor by X% for 5 seconds."
[*]"100% Chance on Potion use to gain X for 10 seconds."
[/list]
[*][b]Effect[/b] – The reward or outcome when the condition is met. Effects vary from simple damage procs to complex utility and game-changing mechanics.[list]
[*]Direct damage (e.g., explosions, chain lightning, projectiles)
[*]Buffs (e.g., increased attack speed, armor, lifesteal)
[*]Summons (e.g., spawning minions or constructs)
[*]Utility (e.g., movement speed, cooldown reduction, damage mitigation)
[/list][/list]
But there are also special relics that come from the hardest content in the game.

[h3]Raidboss Soul Crystals[/h3]
Some of the most powerful Soul Crystals come from the strongest enemies — the raidbosses.

When you defeat a raidboss, it will drop a Soul Crystal containing one of its signature abilities, allowing you to make a devastating boss ability your own.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45068931/e71a124bc8ef8025b08a765ba2f9afbe00aefd87.png[/img]
What makes this system shine is the potential for synergy. Certain conditions and effects naturally complement each other, allowing you to create powerful, chain-triggering setups.


And with that, we wrap up this sneak peek into Sil and the Fading World's Relic & Soul Crystal system! Since the game is still in development, some of the details here may change, but rest assured — we’ll keep you updated every step of the way.

If you haven’t yet, please consider joining our [url=https://discord.com/invite/hmJv5At2e5]Discord Community Server[/url]! It’s a great way to connect with other players, ask questions, and share feedback as we continue building the game together.

Thank you all for being part of this journey with us! ✨❤️
Bardh & Burim

notes.title: [System Spotlight] Itemization
notes.content:
Hello, world!~~ 👋

Welcome to the first post in our System Spotlight series! In this series, we'll be diving into some of the core mechanics that bring Sil and the Fading World to life.

To kick things off, let's explore one of the game's most essential systems: itemization. Sil and the Fading World features a dynamic itemization system inspired by classic ARPGs, offering players significant flexibility to shape their characters to their preferred playstyle. As with most ARPGs, gear in Sil and the Fading World is categorized by rarity, with six distinct levels:

[olist]
[*]Common
[*]Rare
[*]Epic
[*]Heirloom
[*]Legendary
[*]Pure
[/olist] 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45068931/75a0eadc02e703946ede14f37ed56e5775400625.jpg[/img]

[h3]Common Items[/h3]
Common items are the most basic tier, providing only the implicit stats specific to their item type. While simple, they form the foundation for players beginning their journey.

[h3]Rare Items[/h3]
Rare items build upon common items by adding an extra layer: they come with both implicit stats and a randomly rolled suffix and prefix modifier, giving players a taste of customization and potential power.

[h3]Epic Items[/h3]
Epic items always feature at least three modifiers, with an additional random affix or prefix modifier rolled when they drop. Additionally, epic items have a small chance to include one of the powerful Heirloom Modifiers, making them a significant step up in flexibility.

[h3]Heirloom Items[/h3]
Heirloom items are unique and come with their own icon, name, and a distinct heirloom modifier. Alongside this predefined modifier, they roll with two random prefixes, two random suffixes, and an extra random heirloom modifier, offering a high level of customization and uniqueness.

[h3]Legendary Items[/h3]
Legendary items contain unique modifiers that are exclusive to one legendary item in the game, providing effects that can dramatically impact gameplay. For example, a legendary modifier might convert Movement Speed buffs into damage boosts, unlocking new build possibilities. Legendary items also come with five random prefix and suffix modifiers, plus one random Heirloom Modifier.

[h3]Pure Items[/h3]
Pure items represent a rare and prestigious tier, only obtainable in the endgame raiding content. They are the key to creating optimal builds, acting as customizable versions of legendary and heirloom items. While they allow for extensive modification, keep in mind that Pure items are still in development and may undergo further changes.


And with that, we wrap up this sneak peek into Sil and the Fading World's itemization system! Since the game is still in development, some of the details here may evolve, but rest assured, we’ll keep everyone in the loop with any updates.

If you haven’t yet, please consider joining our [url=https://discord.gg/UxxHnffkkJ]Discord Community Server[/url]! 😊 
It's a great way to connect, ask questions, and share feedback as we continue developing the game.

Thank you all for being part of this journey with us! ✨❤️
Bardh & Burim

notes.title: [FAQ] Frequently Asked Questions for Sil and The Fading World
notes.content:
Hello, everyone!~~ 👋

We've been receiving a lot of questions about the game recently, so we want to take a moment to address some of the most frequently asked ones. Here's what you need to know.

[h2]FAQ[/h2]
[b]Is there a demo?[/b]
No there currently isn't a Demo out. We plan to release the Demo in Fall 2024

[b]Is there a Release Date?[/b]
We plan to release into Early Access in 2025

[b]How do I sign up for playtesting?[/b]
We do all testing over Discord you can join [url=https://discord.gg/UxxHnffkkJ]here[/url]

[b]Will the game have controller support?[/b]
The game will feature full controller support on Early Access launch

[b]What were your inspirations?[/b]
The main inspirations were Diablo, Grim Dawn, World of Warcraft and Path of Exile.

[b]Does it support 4K / Ultrawide monitors?[/b]
No

[b]Is there multiplayer or co-op?[/b]
No, the game is singleplayer

Yes once the game launches into Early Access
